Coriolus versicolor (CV), a medicinal mushroom widely consumed in Asian countries, has been demonstrated to be effective in stimulation of immune system and inhibition of tumor growth. The present study aimed to investigate the anti-tumor and anti-metastasis effects of CV aqueous extract in mouse mammary carcinoma 4T1 cells and in 4T1-tumor bearing mouse model.

In vitro treatment of triple-negative breast cancer cells with an extract from the Coriolus versicolor mushroom changes macrophage properties related to tumourigenesis
Our previous results revealed that an extract of the fungus Coriolus versicolor (CV) has anti-cancer and immunomodulatory properties. The aim of the present study was to investigate whether CV extract-treated triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cells can release factors that can reprogram macrophages from pro-tumourigenic to anti-cancer subtypes. RAW 264.7 macrophages were cultured in a conditioned medium (CM) from non-treated 4T1 breast cancer cells (CM-NT) or CV extract-stimulated cells (CM-CV).
